Analytic certainty of network edges (Bayesian Dirichlet-Multinomial)

Source: R/certainty.R
certainty.Rd

certainty() gives each edge of a transition-probability network a posterior mean, standard deviation, credible interval and a decision on whether the edge is certain, all in closed form, and returns them in the layout of bootstrap_network(). It models the outgoing transitions of each state as a Dirichlet-Multinomial process: with a Dirichlet prior of concentration prior, the posterior for state \(i\) is \(\mathrm{Dirichlet}(c_i + \mathrm{prior})\), where \(c_i\) are its transition counts, so each edge probability is marginally Beta. It reads a netobject built with method = "relative", or a netobject_group of them.

With inference = "stability", an edge is certain when the posterior mass outside a band around its weight (consistency_range) is below ci_level; with "threshold", when the mass below edge_threshold is. Certainty says how precisely the observed counts pin an edge down, not whether the edge survives resampling the sequences (bootstrap_network()) or holds across split halves (network_reliability()). Certainty and bootstrap stability agree on homogeneous data. Certainty treats every transition as independent, so it is over-confident when the sequences come from a mixture of latent classes, the more so the longer they are; use bootstrap_network() there.

Usage

certainty(
  x,
  prior = 0.5,
  ci_level = 0.05,
  inference = c("stability", "threshold"),
  consistency_range = c(0.75, 1.25),
  edge_threshold = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'net_certainty'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

x

The network: a netobject built with build_network() using method = "relative" (or its aliases "tna", "transition"), without scaling, or a netobject_group of such networks, each handled on its own. A bare cograph_network is recounted from the sequences it carries, and used only when they reproduce its weights; otherwise, and for an mcml, an error of class nestimate_bad_input is raised. Another method or a scaled network raises an error. For the print() method: a net_certainty object.

prior

The Dirichlet concentration added to every cell of the count matrix, zero cells and self-loops included; a positive number. Default 0.5, the Jeffreys prior.

ci_level

The tail level, in (0, 1), of the equal-tailed credible intervals and of the decision: an edge is certain when its posterior mass (the p_value column) is below it. Default 0.05, a 95% interval. Named to match bootstrap_network().

inference

The decision rule. "stability" (default) takes the posterior mass outside the band consistency_range times the edge's weight; "threshold" takes the posterior mass below edge_threshold.

consistency_range

For inference = "stability": the two multiplicative bounds of the band around each weight, positive numbers in either order. Default c(0.75, 1.25).

edge_threshold

For inference = "threshold": the weight an edge must exceed. Default NULL: the 10th percentile of the non-zero weights. Ignored for "stability".

...

For the print() method: ignored.

Value

For a netobject: a net_certainty object (class c("net_certainty", "net_bootstrap")), so the net_bootstrap methods work on it. print() lists up to five certain edges with the largest absolute posterior means (with their intervals), then the prior, the count of certain edges and the settings; summary() returns one row per non-zero edge with columns from, to, weight, mean, sd, p_value, sig, ci_lower and ci_upper, plus cr_lower and cr_upper (the band) for inference = "stability"; cograph::splot() draws it. The object has the fields of a bootstrap_network() result: original (the input network), mean, sd, p_values, significant (the weights of the certain edges, zero elsewhere), ci_lower, ci_upper, cr_lower, cr_upper (matrices), summary, model (the network of certain edges only), method, params, ci_level, inference, consistency_range and edge_threshold, plus prior, ci_method = "analytic" and iter = NA (no iterations).

For a netobject_group: a named list of those objects, one per network, of class c("net_certainty_group", "net_bootstrap_group", "list"), printed and summarised by the net_bootstrap_group methods (summary() stacks the per-network tables with a group column).

The print() method returns its input invisibly.

Details

Nothing is resampled: the posterior quantities are Beta means, variances and quantiles (stats::qbeta(), stats::pbeta()), so a call takes milliseconds.

References

Johnston, L. & Jendoubi, T. (2026). How Delivery Mode Reshapes Resource Engagement: A Bayesian Differential Network Analysis. TNA Workshop 2026.

See also

bootstrap_network, bayes_compare, network_reliability

Examples

seqs <- data.frame(V1 = c("A","B","A","C","B"), V2 = c("B","C","B","A","C"),
                   V3 = c("C","A","C","B","A"))
net <- build_network(seqs, method = "relative")
cert <- certainty(net)
cert
#> Certainty (Dirichlet)  [Transition Network (relative) | directed]
#>   Prior      : Dirichlet(0.50)  |  Nodes : 3
#>   Edges      : 0 certain / 3 total
#>   CI         : 95%  |  Inference: stability  |  CR [0.75, 1.25]
summary(cert)
#>   from to weight      mean        sd   p_value   sig  ci_lower  ci_upper
#> 1    A  B      1 0.7777778 0.1772720 0.3653545 FALSE 0.3485528 0.9927924
#> 2    B  C      1 0.8181818 0.1512819 0.2740159 FALSE 0.4405413 0.9943896
#> 3    C  A      1 0.7777778 0.1772720 0.3653545 FALSE 0.3485528 0.9927924
#>   cr_lower cr_upper
#> 1     0.75     1.25
#> 2     0.75     1.25
#> 3     0.75     1.25
